title: Homotopy density of small presentable cofibrant objects
statement:
Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence, cofibrant-object and Reedy terminology of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A model category is combinatorial when its underlying category is locally presentable and its two weak factorization systems have small generating sets. An object is $\lambda$-presentable if its ordinary Hom functor preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits; $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone. Locally $\lambda$-presentable means generated under these colimits by a small family of $\lambda$-presentable objects. Use homotopy colimits of [lem-coef-hocolim-reindexing-zigzags], computed by the colimit of a projectively cofibrant replacement. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial and let $\lambda$ be an infinite regular cardinal such that $\mathcal M$ is locally $\lambda$-presentable, $\lambda$-filtered colimits preserve objectwise weak equivalences, and there is a functorial cofibrant replacement preserving $\lambda$-presentable objects. Choose a small full representative category $C$ of the cofibrant $\lambda$-presentable objects. For each $X\in\mathcal M$, let $(C\downarrow X)$ have objects $(c,u:c\to X)$ and arrows $a:c\to c'$ with $u'a=u$, and let $V_X(c,u)=c$. Then the canonical augmentation
$$\operatorname{hocolim}_{(C\downarrow X)}V_X\longrightarrow X$$
is a weak equivalence. The assertion holds for all $X$, without a fibrancy assumption.
